turnaround_reason: Beauty conglomerate crushed from ~$12 to ~$2.6 on Consumer Beauty underperformance, slowing prestige fragrance, and a heavy debt load; interim CEO Markus Strobel (ex-P&G) is running a turnaround after Sue Nabi's exit.
bullish_points: Sold the Gucci Beauty license back to Kering for ~$400M ($250M cash upfront), proceeds earmarked for debt reduction; net leverage now near a decade low
CoverGirl and Sally Hansen closing the sellout gap vs market per interim CEO
Optically cheap: forward P/E ~10, P/B 0.77, EV/EBITDA ~7.4
Small insider buys near current price (CFO Mercier at $2.65, officer von Bretten 83k shares at $2.41 early 2026)
bearish_points: Withdrew FY2026 guidance after Q2 and CEO departure — visibility is poor
Still $3.3B total debt against a $2.3B market cap; current ratio 0.755 (weak liquidity)
Operating margin -2.4%, profit margin -10.4%; like-for-like revenue -3%
Securities class-action lawsuits and management turnover add overhang
catalyst: Next earnings print showing deleveraging traction and Consumer Beauty stabilization; Gucci second payment ($150M) by Sep 2027
suggested_trade: Pass or tiny spot only — too levered until deleveraging and share stabilization are proven
key_risk: Debt load plus withdrawn guidance; Consumer Beauty keeps losing share and leverage stays elevated
would_skip_if: Leverage does not come down materially or Consumer Beauty continues bleeding share
